units.title: Counting Numbers: 1-10

outcomes.text: Count by 1s (forwards and backwards) to 10
Represent the number of objects in a group with a written numeral 0 to 10.
Count to answer “how many” questions (up to 5); Given a number to 5, count out how many objects
Identify, compare and order groups of 1 to 5 objects
Demonstrate an understanding of the relative size of numbers1 to 5, quickly naming a number that is 1 more or less than a number to 5, and solve related word problems (orally)
Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction by quickly naming a number that is 1 more or less than a number to 5
Demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns by duplicating and extending element sound or action pattern

resources: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

units.title: Counting How Many: 1-10

outcomes.text: Count on or backwards from any number between 1 and 10

Duplicate and extend 3 element sound or action pattern

steps.text: Have pupils duplicate and extend 2- or 3-element repeating number patterns. Write a 2-element repeating number pattern on board, e.g., 1, 1, 2; 1, 1, 2; 1, 1, 2; ….

Jiciik únokooruwab wariiboorumi di síbukaas sooluul banjaat di jiliik sipinaas sammi di únokoorumaw wariiboorumi, banjaat di jípajul sipinaas salanlankenimi banjaat nuciik sipinaas soone 5 siceenas saatumi ebiley sariiboorumi
Put another, now a 3-element repeating number pattern on board, e.g., 5, 7, 7, 5; 5 7, 7; 5, 7, …)

Jiciik únokooruwab wariiboorumi di síbukaas sooluul banjaat di jiliik sipinaas sammi di únokoorumaw wariiboorumi, banjaat di jípajul sipinaas salanlankenimi banjaat nuciik sipinaas soone 5 siceenas saatumi ebiley sariiboorumi

lessons.title: Counting forwards and backwards from 1 to 10
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Count numbers from 1 to 10 forwards and backwards in Soninke and in English.

activities.title: Counting Numbers: 1-10 in L1
activities.title_nl: Epiney sipinaas yákon bee uñen di kújoolaak

steps.text: Hang Numeral Cards (A5 size) from 1 to 10 on a number line or write the numbers on the board; point and have pupils count with you..

Ínje bee eñuur sipinaas yákon yákon, étooŋum di yákon, jipinaal síñakon di ereg yákon, sigaba, sífeejiir,, sibaciir, futok, futok di yákon, futok di sigaba, futok di sífeejiir futok di sibaciir, uñen..
Have 2 or 3 individual pupils to do it; then have all pupils do it with you. Repeat the activity with the numbers written on the board.
Repeat the activity counting backwards from 10 in the L1
Jipinaal bálamuk di étooŋum uñen, futok di sibaciir, futok di sifeejiir, futok di sigaba, futok di yákon, futok , sibaciir, sifeejiir, sigaba, yákon ñetum di kújoolaak
Have pupils do activities in G1PB Activity 1.1.2 in NL .

activities.title: Counting Numbers to 10 in English
activities.title_nl: Epiney sipinaas bee 10 di English

steps.text: Hang Numeral Cards (A5 size) from 1 to 10 on a number line or write the numbers on the board; point and have pupils count with you.
Ínje bee ñuur sipinaas yákon yákon, étooŋum di 10, wulaal búrom uregaal ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one ñetum di Ingiliisey.
Have 2 or 3 individual pupils to do it; then have all pupils do it with you. Repeat the activity with the numbers written on the board.
Repeat the activity using number names in both L1/L2; pointing and having pupils to count by saying both the L1/L2 counting numbers.E.g, yákon, one; sigaba, two; futok, five; etc
Have pupils do G1PB Activities 1.1.1 and 1.1.2 in L1 & L2.

closure.assessment: Take learners to G1PB Activity1.1.2 and ask them to point to a number you call out and count the number of hops the dog will make to reach the number moving forward. Repeat the activity for the hops the rabbit will take moving backwards.

lessons.title: Clap Numbers and count to find “how many”
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: clap and count numbers called out from 1 to 10 in their SONINKE and in English.
count to find “how many” are in a given group of objects or counters
materials: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

activities.title: Play “Clap that number”
activities.title_nl: Fáreed fati ‘’Jileew epinaay uye

steps.text: Put Numeral Cards from 1 to 10 on a table or write the numbers on the board; point and have pupils clap with you.
Wulaal bee eleew sipinaas; Ínje bee ewonk epina, ibanjaat muyuul di jileew yo
Wulaal bee ebil eleew sipinaas sammi di wayitaw wati sipinaas. ÿar kayitak kati epinaay ubanjaat nuleew epinaay yantomi
Have groups of pupils in rows go in turns to pick and clap a number; and have all pupils do it with you.
Have pupils clap the dots for the numbers in G1PB Activity 1.1.2.

activities.title: Play “How many?”
activities.title_nl: fáreed ‘butumbuu’?

steps.text: Put items up to 5 (pencils, books, pens, cards, sticks, etc. on a table) and identify things not more than 5 in the classroom and corner shop, e.g., girls in a row, boys in a row, windows, books on the table, legs of the teacher’s table, tins/boxes in the corner shop.
Choose (or Point) to a group of items on the table, e.g., books, and have pupils count with you.
Wulaal bee pin ban nuñesaal síbukaas soone butumbuu soom di taabuley. Wulaal búrom jipinaal yákon, sigaba, sífeejiir…..
Síbukaas sigaba sonto.
Write the numeral on the board, and ask the pupils to write it in their jotters.
Jiciik epinaay di síbukaas sooluul.
Have pupils play the “How Many game” with objects.
Have pupils do G1PB Activity 1.1.3.

closure.assessment: Take learners to G1PB Activity1.1.4 and count to tell the number.
closure.homework: Ask pupils to count how many people are in their house (or family).

lessons.title: Put objects into groups of 2, 3, 4 or 5 and identify number in a group
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: stand in (or put objects in) groups of 2, 3, 4 or 5.
identify objects put in groups of 2, 3 …, 10
materials: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

activities.title: Play “Stand in Groups of 2, 3, 4 or 5s”
activities.title_nl: Fáreed “Jijuum kúguut kati 2, 3, 4, mba 5”

steps.text: Take pupils into play ground (or an open space) and have them walk around.
Wulaal bee ebil fáreed fati ejuumey yati kúguutak kati kugaba kugaba, kúfeejiir kúfeejiir, kubaciir kubaciir mba futok futok. Iwonkujat epinaay di jijuum kúguutak kati sipinaas san iwonkumi
Repeat the activity using the Jola number names for the sizes of the groups.

activities.title: Play “Finding 2s, 3s, 4s … 10s
activities.title_nl: Eñesey yati

steps.text: Have pupils count out loud each group of objects found in the Soninke and then in Soninke. Call out a number (2 to 10) and have pupils look for the objects in that quantity and count out loud the objects.
Jijiker Jiŋomen di kalaasey man jípajul wahaw wan kupinak kooliwo sireewoorumi di sipinaas sani iwonkumi. Jipin wahaw di kújoolaak man jíYísen mante epinaay yawonkumi ecila.
Repeat the activity with objects in the classroom corner shop
Repeat the activity with objects in pictures on the wall.
Have pupils play the “How Many game” with objects in Unit 1.1.3 of G1PB Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.1.4.

closure.assessment: Display groups of objects on a table up to 10 (e.g., pencils, books, pens, cards, sticks, etc.) and have learners to count in unison in groups to say how many.
closure.homework: Ask pupils to count how many pets (or animals) are in their house (or family).

lessons.title: Matching Groups of Counters with Fingers Displayed and Numerals
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: count out counters that match the number of fingers displayed in the air
match numerals cards with numbers shown by objects (or card)

activities.title: Play “Show me ___” numbers 1 to 5 with counters
activities.title_nl: Fáreed‘ yísom…….’ Sipinaas 1 bee 5 di mupinumaam

steps.text: Call out a number. Pupils count out that number of counters on their desk (or show that many fingers in the air). Then have pupils play game in pairs.
Wulaal bee ebil fáreed; ‘ínje bee ewonk epinaay, banjaat muyuul bee epin epinaay eciila ñetum mupinumaam man jíyisom.
Have pupils play the game in pairs. One calls out number, other counts out counters; then both write the number in their jotter.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.1.5.

activities.title: Play “What number is this?” with numerals 1 to 5
activities.title_nl: Fáreed “Epinaay uye yéy ma?’ di sipinaas 1 bee 5

steps.text: Pick/point to a number card with objects (or on chalkboard) and say the number without counting. Split the class into groups.

Wulaal bee ebil Fáreed. Añiil ákon di kúguutak kooluul aŋar kákon kákon kati epinaay wan áYísen ban nareg wahaw wooni butumbuu wantomi bapinut. . Kanjaat man uregum moo, nusof kayitak. Fúguutaf fasomumi wayitaw juup foo fuwuujumi.

closure.assessment: Display number and numeral cards 1 to 10 face up. Have pair of learners come to the table, one picks and show the class a number card and other picks and shows class the matching numeral card.

lessons.title: Making Groups of Counters to Find Which is More/Less
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: count out counters that match the number of fingers displayed in the air
match numerals cards with numbers shown by objects (or card)

activities.title: Which of two numbers is more?
activities.title_nl: Sipinaas use sigabaas yéy efaŋe?

steps.text: Give pupils two numbers – e.g., 4 & 2. Have them work with a partner to take counters that represent each of the two numbers; and then identify which group of counters is more and justify their answer.
Ínje bee ewonk sipina soone sigaba. Aw di apaali jiŋar mupinumaam mati epina yánosani banjaat di jipajul epinaay yafaŋumi ban di jíYísen waawu ukaane man kaan moo.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.1.6.

activities.title: Play “Make a group with more/less than this number”
activities.title_nl: Fáreed “Joonen fúguut fafaŋumi epinaay uye mba fan epinaay uye efaŋumi.”

steps.text: Have each pupils make a group of counters (1 – 5). Call out a number and have them compare to see whether their groups are more/less than the number called out.
Make sure each pupil has counters up to 5 on their tables. Ask each pupil to make any group of counters (1 – 5).
Jirok di apaali man jijoonen kúguut kati mupinumaam.
Ínje bee ebil ewonk epinaay. Jinaamen man jijuk mante fúguutaf fati mupinumaam mooluul mufaŋe mba mupinumaam mooluul mufaŋe man mutiitiye epinaay yan eetumi bee ewonkey.
Have 2 or 3 pupils (one acting as teacher) go to the front of the class to repeat the activity. Go over activity with whole class.

closure.assessment: Display 3 pairs of counters on the table, one of each pair should be 1 or 2 more than the other. Have learners come to the table to determine which is more and explain.
closure.homework: Ask learners to count tea-cups and spoons in their home to find which is more.

lessons.title: 1 Finding objects in groups of 2, 3, 4, …, 10 in the classroom
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: recognize objects in groups of 2, 3, 4, …, 10 in and around the classroom

activities.title: Play “Finding 5s, 6s, 7s, 8s or 9s”
activities.title_nl: Eñesey 5s, 6s,7s, 8s mba 9s

steps.text: Have pupils count out loud each group of objects (from 5 to 9) found in the Soninke and then in English.
Call out a number (5 to 9).
Jijiker jiŋomen di kalaasey man jípajul wahaw wan kupinak kooli wo sireewoorumi di epinaay yawonkumi. Jipin wahaw di kújoolaak bee manj mante epinaay yawonkumi yo.
Repeat the activity with objects in the classroom corner shop
Repeat the activity with objects in pictures on the wall.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.1

closure.assessment: Take pupils to G1PB Activities 1.1.2 and point to the dot numbers for numbers you call, e.g., 5, 3, 7, etc.

lessons.title: Finding objects in groups of 2, 3, 4, …, 10 in the classroom
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: count to find in SONINKE “how many” in a group of objects in and around the classroom

activities.title: Play “How many?”
activities.title_nl: Fáreed fati ‘’butumbuu’’?

steps.text: Put items up to 10 (pencils, books, pens, cards, sticks, etc. on a table, tins/boxes in the corner shop) and identify things not more than 10 in the classroom which all pupils can see, e.g., girls in a row, boys in a row, windows, books on the table, legs of the teacher’s table.
Wulaal bee ebil epiney bee ñes ‘’síbuka soone butumbuu soom di taabuley.” Wulaal búrom upinaal di ereg yákon, sigaba, sífeejiir......
Jiciik epinaay di síbukaas sooluul.
Write the numeral on the board, and ask the pupils to write it in their jotters Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.1.

lessons.title: Before-before/After-after game
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: state the number that comes before and after a number called.

activities.title: “Before-before/After-after game”
activities.title_nl: Fáreed fati “Balaa mba wuujujaat

steps.text: We play the game standing and you respond Before when I say Before-before. When I call out a number you identify the number that comes before that number and say it. Anyone who calls the wrong number is out of the game and must sit down. Allow pupils to look at number line to find answer.
Balaa-balaa/balaa:
i. 3 → sigaba;
ii. 6 → futok;
iii. 8 → futok di sigaba; etc
Repeat the came for After-after. When I call out a number you identify the number that comes after that number and say it. Anyone who calls the wrong number is out of the game and must sit down.
Wuujujaat-wuujujaat/wuujujaat:
i. 3 → sibaciir;
ii. 6 → futok di sigabaa;
iii. 8 →; etc. futok di sibaciir
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.3.

lessons.title: Ordering numerals 5 to 9
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: stand in the “order” of the numbers 5 to 9.

activities.title: Play “Stand in Order” Numbers between 5 and 10
activities.title_nl: Fáreed fati “Jijuum riiboor” nan sipinaas sammi titooraay yati 5 di 10

steps.text: Put 3 numbers on the board in random order. Say work with a partner to arrange the numbers from smallest to largest and justify the solution to the class. Place numeral cards between 5 and 10 turned upside down on a table.

Wulaal bee ebil fáreed “Jijuum riibenoor” ínje bee ewonk kuñiil koone kúfeejiir di fúguut fanosani man kuŋar wayitaw wati sipinaas; jijiker sipinaas man jijuum jiriiboor kátooŋum epinaay yatiitiyaay di bamoyab bee yafaŋumi kákalaa di báridab banjaat di jíYísen wayitaw. [Group with correct order or arrangement wins a point]
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.2 and 1.2.3

closure.assessment: Display numeral card (5 to 9) facing down. Ask learners to go in turns in groups of 4 to pick any four of the cards and arrange themselves in positions from smallest (left) to largest (right).

lessons.title: Compare two numbers using the More/less than Relation
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: stand in the “order” of the numbers 5 to 9.

activities.title: More or less than comparison story problems
activities.title_nl: Kafaŋaak mba katiitiyak ñetum kasankenak

steps.text: Give pupils situations shown below.
Awa kumanga koone 8 naake. Buuba koone 6 naake. Waawu nuŋoolen uregom?
Encourage pupils to describe the situation by comparing. Examples of expected responses are:
Awa aakumi wajuupo’aaw
Awa nafaŋenumi Buuba kugaba.
Awa naakennaaken afaŋen Buuba jayinkun
Buuba kumanga kupinaay nabaje
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.2.4 and 1.2.5.

closure.assessment: Display numeral card (5 to 9) facing down. Ask learners to go in turns in pairs to pick a card each and show it to the class. Ask each to make a statement using the more/less than to compare the two numbers.
closure.homework: Ask learners to count the number of people in their family (or household) who are male and female. Then ask them to make a statement using the more/less than to compare the number of males and females.

lessons.title: Finding the rules for Sorting Objects into Groups
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Find different ways of comparing object based on size, color, shape, etc
Compare and order groups of up to 10 objects

activities.title: Finding the rules for sorting objects into groups
activities.title_nl: Eñesey sílingaas sati kápajulak kati wahaw ukaan wo di kúguutak.

steps.text: Present pupils with a collection of 3D objects of different types and colours; also, collections from the classroom corner shop.

Say: Kaan kúguutak kati wahaw wayesoorumi. Yísen sílingaas sati wahaw wayesoorumi mba waawu ukaane man wahaw wayesoorumi úguuti. Pin wahaw woone butumbuu woom di kúguutak kanaamutumi banjaat di jiciik epinaay di síbukaas sooluul (mba poop di bulakubootey)
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activity 1.3.1

closure.assessment: Give learners objects of different color and ask the learner to sort the objects based on color.

lessons.title: Creating the rules for sorting shapes into groups
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Describe relative size of 1 to 10 objects
Compare and order groups of up to 10 objects
materials: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

activities.title: Creating the rules for sorting 2D cutout shapes into groups
activities.title_nl: Kajoonenak kati sílingaas sati éguutey yati utingumaw wati únokoorumaw di kúguutak.

steps.text: Have pupils sort sort 2D cutout shapes of the same sizes into groups and describe the rule used.
Display a collection of small and large 2D cutout geometric shapes (i.e., 3-sided shapes, 4-sided shapes and round shapes).

Kaan kúguutak kati únokoorumaw wayesoorumi. Yísen sílingaas sati éguutey mba waawu ukaane man wahaw wayesoorumi úguuti. Jipin wahaw woone butumbuu woom di kúguutak kanaamutumi banjaat di jiciik epinaay di síbukaas sooluul (mba poop di bulakubootey mba di kacaakak)
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.3.2

closure.assessment: Give learners objects of different color and size, ask the learner to sort the objects into different groups and state how the sorting is done.
closure.homework: Ask pupils to find objects at home that look like shapes (e.g., plate, book, box, lid). They should sort them into groups: • Round shapes • 3-sided shapes • 4-sided shapes

lessons.title: Finding 5s, 6s, 7s, 8s or 9s
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Represent number of objects in group (6 to 10) with numeral
Build a set (or a group) that has 1 more (or less) than a number between 5 and 10
materials: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

activities.title: Play “Finding 5s, 6s, 7s, 8s or 9s”
activities.title_nl: Eñesey 5s, 6s, 7s, 8s 9s

steps.text: Have pupils count out loud each group of objects (from 5 to 9) found in the Soninke and then in Soninke.
Call out a number (5 to 9).
Jijiker jiŋomen di kalaasey man jípajul wahaw wan kupinak kooliwo siremi di epinaay yan iwonkumi. Jipin wahaw di kújoolaak man jijuk mante epinaay yawonkimi yoo.
Repeat the activity with objects in the classroom corner shop
Repeat the activity with objects in pictures on the wall.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.3.3

closure.assessment: Ask pupils to look around the home and find groups of: 5 objects, 6 objects, 7 objects, 8 objects, 9 objects Example: books, windows, shoes, pencils, bottle tops
closure.homework: Ask pupils to play a counting game with a family member: • One person calls a number from 5–9. • The pupil finds that number of objects and counts them aloud

lessons.title: Ordering Numbers
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Compare and order groups of up to 10 objects
materials: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

activities.title: Play “Stand in Order” with numbers from 6 to 10
activities.title_nl: Fáreed fati “Jijuum Riiboor”

steps.text: Put 3 numbers on the board in random order.
Jirok di apaali man jinen sipinaas siriiboor kápurum di yayinkunaay bee yáamakey ban nureg kalaasey buu nukammi eeno
Place numeral cards between 5 and 10 turned upside down on a table to play the “Stand in Order” game.

Wulaal bee ebil fáreed “jijuum jiriiboor” ínje bee ewonk kuñiil koone kúfeejiir di fúguut fanoosani man anoosani aŋar kayitak kati epinaay; jijiker sipinaas man jijuum riiboor di katooŋumi epinaay yatiitiyaay di bamoyab bee yafaŋumi kákalaa di báridab banjaat di jíyisen wayitaw wooluul.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activity 1.3.4

closure.assessment: Pupils make small number cards from 5 to 10 using paper or cardboard. They can play in pairs or groups • Picking 3 cards • Arranging the numbers from smallest to largest
closure.homework: Have learners copy and complete the number order in their jotter a. 5, __, 7, __, 9, __ b. __, 6, 7, __, 9, 10 etc.

lessons.title: Comparing number of objects
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Compare groups of objects
Describe relative size of 1 to 10 objects

activities.title: More or less than comparison story problems
activities.title_nl: Kafaŋaak mba katiitiyak di kanoolen kati burokab bati kanamenak

steps.text: Give pupils situations shown below.
Awa kumanga koone 5 naake. Buuba koone 7 naake. Waawu nuŋoolene uregom?
Encourage pupils to describe the situation by comparing. Examples of expected responses are:
Buuba aakumi kajuupo'aak
Buuba nafaŋenumi Awa kugaba.
Buuba jajinkun nafaŋene Awa
Awa kumanga kupinaay nabaje
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activity 1.3.5

closure.assessment: Give the learners the story problem and have them answer the questions that follow: Mariama has 8 sweets and Lamin has 6 sweets.
closure.homework: Questions: • Who has more sweets? • Who has fewer sweets? • How many more sweets does Mariama have? Parents can help pupils complete to complete the following in their jotter • 7 oranges is ___ than 5 oranges. • 4 pencils is ___ than 6 pencils. • 9 books is ___ than 8 books. (Expected answers: more, less/fewer, more) Partitioning Numbers

lessons.title: Partitioning (Numbers 5, 6 and 7) into 2
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Partition numbers (5, 6 and 7) into 2 groups
Count the numbers in each group
materials: counters (e.g., sticks, seeds, beads or bottle caps)

activities.title: Partitioning (Numbers 5, 6 and 7) into 2
activities.title_nl: Ecaabey sipinaas ( 5, 6 di 7) di ucaab ugaba

steps.text: Give pupils a number (5, 6 or 7), for example 6; have them count that number of counters and find the different ways of partitioning them into 2 groups. E.g., 5, is a group of 2 counters and a group of 3 counters”, i.e., 5 is (2, 3). Ask if they can find another different way of partitioning it?
Wulaal bee ebil eñes kútaagul kanaamut kati ecaabey sipinaas ukaan kúguut ugaba;. ÿar mupina moone 6 man ukaan mo di kúguut ugaba ban nureg fanoosani butumbuu éndo.
Have pupils take the 6 counters and find another way of partitioning it into two groups?
Ñes burunŋ buceen bati ecaabey yati mupinuma moone 6 ukaan mo kúguut
2. Jiñes burunŋ wuceen.
Repeat activity with another number, say 7 and 8.
Have pupils do the activities in G1PB Activities 1.4.1 to 1.4.3

closure.assessment: Find another way of partitioning 7 counters into 2 groups
closure.homework: Have learners to partition 8 counters into 2 groups. Find the other ways?

lessons.title: Play “What can you tell me about…?” numbers 6 to 9
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Describe numbers (6 to 9) by relating them to the size of other numbers on the number line
materials: counters (e.g., sticks, seeds, beads or bottle caps)

activities.title: Play “What can you tell me about…?” numbers 6 to 9
activities.title_nl: Fáreed “Waawu jiŋoolene jiregom mati ………?” di sipinaas 6 bee 9

steps.text: Describe a number by relating it to the sizes of other numbers using the number line. Encourage pupils to describe relative size of number by looking at the number line.

Wulaal bee káyisen epina di kanaamenak kati man sipinaas saasu sifaŋoorumi eeno di kujuumak kooli so di baka kakaacerak acerab nan: 7 pan íyísen nan: -7 yoo yommi titooraay yati 6 di 8 -7 efaŋe kákaala 5 bare efaŋe katiiti 10. -7 yákon efaŋumi 6 -7 sigaba efaŋumi 5 etc
Encourage pupils to describe relative size of number by looking at the number line. Challenge partners to come up with as many different statements as possible about the number
Repeat the activity for another number, say 8, then 9, etc.

closure.assessment: Ask learners to describe 6 by relating it to the size of other numbers on the number line
closure.homework: Ask learners to describe 10 by relating it to the size of other numbers on the number line

lessons.title: How many altogether - sums less than 10
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Put pairs of numbers whose sum is less than 10
materials: counters (e.g., sticks, seeds, beads or bottle caps)

activities.title: Play “How many altogether” sums less than 10
activities.title_nl: Fáreed “Búrom butumbuu” san banampenerab búriiŋutumi 10

steps.text: Put a pair of numbers (whose sum is less than 10) on the board (or no cards) in random order. Have pupils work with a partner using counters to find the pair of numbers together make that number.
